title: MuKo Home V9 access-face and use-position audit
scope: kitchen sink, cooktop, dishwasher, refrigerator, and upper cabinets
living media storage and mobile television parking
balcony laundry, basket, housekeeping cabinet, and upper storage

coordinateAndEvidenceRules.coordinates: x/z are plan axes in metres; y is height above floor in metres
coordinateAndEvidenceRules.frontConvention: wall_storage fronts are local -z in storage-mesh.ts; model groups rotate by -rotation degrees, so world face is derived from that transform
coordinateAndEvidenceRules.humanEnvelope: Where calculated, uses the existing fixed 0.45 m radius / 1.88 m height concept cylinder. This is a conservative model envelope, not a code requirement or measured body study.

evidenceLevels.source_geometry: values and orientation are present in the current model source
evidenceLevels.static_envelope_calculation: derived from nominal model bounds without doors, posture, or manipulation
evidenceLevels.motion_sampling: only present where an existing test explicitly sweeps that part; this audit did not add or run new motion tests
evidenceLevels.human_use_unverified: reach, stance, posture, carrying, or simultaneous use lacks an adequate current model/test

coordinateAndEvidenceRules.fieldAndOriginalPlan: Dimensions are concept model values, not site measurements. The project retains the sink and cooktop positions already corrected against the user's original plan. This isolated access audit did not independently reopen that plan; its station-overlap calculation is not a reason by itself to undo the source-based correction.

findings.status: current V9 geometry matches requested access direction
findings.selectedAccessFace: +x long side toward entry corridor; -x is the back; +/-z are short end panels
findings.evidence: home-design.ts explicitly declares accessFace +x and accessFrom entry_left_corridor; reconstructed parts omit the +x long panel while retaining the -x back, both end panels, shelves, and top. This corrects the earlier short-end access interpretation.
findings.noChangeBasis: The requested long side is open to the foyer and can be approached at nominal station (5.85,7.875). The structural column is centered at (5.15,6.175), with its north face z=6.425 and the island south end z=7.425; the 1.0 m longitudinal separation keeps the modeled approach from crossing the column envelope.
findings.nextAcceptance: Sample the final entryReturn mesh/collisionParts together with the full flip-up hatch from 0–100%, then test a standing 0.45 m-radius approach and hand reach to each shelf. Hinge hardware remains concept-only.

findings.status: static two-person station conflict under the existing avatar envelope

selectedAccessFaces.cooktopRun: +z (main run front at z≈4.13 after 180° group rotation)

calculatedConflict.interpretation: the two 0.45 m plan circles substantially overlap; current coordinates cannot establish two people using the sink and cooktop simultaneously without occupying the same stance area

findings.noChangeBasis: Sink and cooktop locations are the positions already corrected against the user's original plan and retained by the V9 brief. Keep that source-based placement; the circle overlap only flags that two separate 0.45 m-radius operators at these nominal stations are not jointly demonstrated. Do not infer that the source correction is wrong or move either fixture from this isolated access calculation.
findings.nextAcceptance: Render the two station circles over all base cabinets and door states; test a one-person sequence and at least one two-person alternative with unchanged body radii. Preserve the source-corrected fixture placement unless new source evidence changes it.

findings.area: 厨房冰箱、洗碗机与厨房门
findings.status: joint access and simultaneous operation not verified

dishwasher.basis: 0.45 m in front of sampled open-door max z≈4.87

fridge.basis: 0.45 m west of nominal world front x≈3.89

findings.calculatedConflict: Existing model/test data shows dishwasher-open visible bounds extend to z≈4.87, while fridge has a 110° leaf and 0.55 m drawer travel. No current test combines the fridge door/drawer, dishwasher door, kitchen door leaf, and two standing bodies in one state; no full collision is claimed.
findings.noChangeBasis: Nominal appliance positions are preserved; the model reports them as concept dimensions. Current data does not support moving appliances or claiming two-user clearance.
findings.nextAcceptance: Sample fridge door and drawer independently and together with the dishwasher and kitchen door. Add a 0.45 m-radius person at each front and identify whether at least one safe stance remains without blocking the other operator.

findings.area: 主卧衣柜、床对面一字工作台与两把办公椅
findings.status: source geometry and 101-step chair-retreat AABB checks support a static inline candidate; actual person/door/wardrobe use remains unverified
findings.selectedAccessFace: +x, inferred from front panel at x≈7.591 and wardrobe placement against the west room edge

doorLeafConservativeEnvelope.method: AABB covering either side of the 0.88 m leaf quarter-turn around hinge [6.9,1.885]

calculatedConflict.sampledStaticEvidence: tests/v9-space.spec.ts samples both chairs through 101 poses from tucked to 350 mm retreated against the bed frame, wardrobe, the conservative door-edge envelope, and each other; zero plan AABB overlap is asserted
calculatedConflict.interpretation: the 0.45 m-radius circle is 0.14 m wider than the 0.76 m wardrobe-side gap; this is only a failed conservative circle-envelope check and does not establish ordinary standing or wardrobe use as impossible. The chair-path sample is static furniture geometry, not a person, open-wardrobe, or actual door-motion test

findings.noChangeBasis: The selected preference is one 2.6 x 0.75 m straight desk run opposite the intact 1800 x 2000 mm mattress, with PC at x=8.6 and Mac at x=9.9. Both unchanged 0.67 x 0.65 m chairs retreat 350 mm; the existing static test samples this motion against frame, wardrobe, and a conservative door-edge envelope. The 0.565 m chair-to-bed gap and 0.63 m between chair footprints do not meet a 0.90 m-radius-expanded circulation target, so two-person passage is not passed.
findings.nextAcceptance: Add the actual full-scale 0.45 m-radius user(s), task-posture/turning envelopes, bed linen, wardrobe door/drawer opening, and hinged master-door animation; verify simultaneous use and exit with the full-scale chairs. Keep results as static-only until that combined scenario is tested.

findings.status: static approach appears possible; door and converted-bed use remain unverified
findings.selectedAccessFace: -x, inferred from cabinetPaint front at x≈4.009 and 180° wall-storage conventions

calculatedConflict.interpretation: static envelope leaves enough nominal width for one 0.45 m-radius circle, but wardrobe door swing, bedding, and guest entry route are absent

findings.noChangeBasis: The modeled gap has 0.28 m beyond the conservative person diameter; no fixed-envelope collision was found in this cross-check. Preserve current geometry pending door/bed test.
findings.nextAcceptance: Sample folded and fully opened bed with bedding, wardrobe door leaf, room entry door, and one person approaching the wardrobe; include nightstand and stored bedding state.

findings.area: 水吧与下柜/台面下空间
findings.status: selected fronts face the working side; this is storage/preparation space, not a two-person knee counter

selectedAccessFaces.entryReturn: +x per the corrected V9 access-face contract

findings.calculatedConflict: No separate knee-space or seated pair of users is encoded; bar-role metadata explicitly excludes two-person knee seating. Shelf access is represented as fixed geometry, while cabinet doors, appliance retrieval, and a standing operator are not joined in one sampled scene.
findings.noChangeBasis: Keep the counter dedicated to coffee/preparation/storage and retain the +x foyer-facing entry return. Do not infer a seat from open lower volume or from the small 900 mm flip-up hatch.
findings.nextAcceptance: Check every front and open cavity at full-size against a standing 1.88 m body, appliance doors, hatch, and the parked/deployed dining set; confirm actual hand reach and outlet/water service locations.

findings.status: lowered in V9; reach/use remains an ergonomic candidate, not a person test

calculatedConflict.interpretation: daily storage is lowered from the previous 1.70–2.60 m band; upper shelf/hanging-glass reach and head/hand clearance still lack anthropometric or reach-envelope validation

findings.noChangeBasis: V9 already lowers the three bar upper units to y=1.52 and keeps frequently handled items in an open center bay. Reserve the highest shelf for light/occasional display until the 188 cm user's comfortable reach and standing head envelope are sampled.
findings.nextAcceptance: Use the fixed-height 1.88 m avatar with reach arms and the actual 0.45 m body envelope; test cup retrieval and door/open-front use without altering avatar scale. Verify hanging glasses do not occupy the user's head/forearm path.

findings.area: 玄关日常洞洞板与高位季节柜
findings.status: daily-use open shelf and loose hooks are replaced by a lower pegboard; high cabinet remains seasonal and reach/door interaction is not measured

selectedAccessFaces.dailyPegboard: -z, facing foyer; replaces upper-entry-display and bag-hooks

findings.calculatedConflict: The pegboard panel is at y=1.24–1.88 m with its nominal access face toward -z. Hook projection and actual bag/key retrieval geometry are not modeled. The separate upper-entry cabinet starts at y=2.02 and ends at 2.60 m and remains classified seasonal.
findings.noChangeBasis: The source overlay removes upper-entry-display and bag-hooks and adds entry-pegboard at x=7.3,z=8.29,y=1.24,w=0.82,h=0.64, replacing the daily-item location; the high cabinet remains for low-frequency items. No claim is made about fixing substrate capacity or the loaded hooks' clearance.
findings.nextAcceptance: Check key and light-bag retrieval with the entrance door and hatch in actual states; confirm screw substrate and hook load, and test that a loaded bag does not protrude into the entry passage. Keep heavy/daily items out of the high cabinet unless measured reach supports them.

findings.area: 阳台家政柜与内置洗衣篮
findings.status: basket is assigned to the cabinet's lower-left bay; approach circle has nominal static clearance, but retrieval and cabinet-door interaction remain unverified

calculatedConflict.interpretation: the basket is parked inside the cabinet footprint in its lower-left bay and is separated from the nominal approach circle by about 65 mm in plan. This is a simple static rectangle/circle check only; an open cabinet front, actual basket withdrawal, and a person retrieving it are not modeled

findings.noChangeBasis: The final overlay removes the fixed sorting/folding table, parks the 0.30 x 0.50 m basket in the housekeeping cabinet's lower-left bay, and assigns clean-laundry folding to the stowed/deployed dining table. The approach is no longer statically blocked by the basket, but its retrieval path and cabinet door state are not yet coupled.
findings.nextAcceptance: Model the actual lower-left cabinet opening and basket withdrawal with a fixed 0.45 m-radius person; verify the path from cabinet to dining table and back, including other balcony appliances and cabinet contents. Do not treat the 65 mm static separation as an operational clearance result.

findings.area: 阳台洗烘机、吊顶晾衣架与上柜
findings.status: faces align with balcony aisle; loaded and simultaneous use not verified

selectedAccessFaces.upperLaundry: +z above machine; removed by V9 overlay

findings.calculatedConflict: Balcony interior width is nominally 1.20 m; a 0.45 m-radius circle centered at x=12.25 leaves 0.15 m to each side wall. V9 removes upper-laundry, but washer/dryer doors, basket handling, and any hanging garments are not modeled as one human-use state. The overhead rack nominal plane is y=2.35 m, 0.47 m above the 1.88 m body top before adding garments or a raised arm.
findings.noChangeBasis: Appliance fronts face the open balcony aisle, and the standing body nominally fits the bare 1.20 m width. Keep the V9 removal of the machine-top cabinet; do not infer loaded-laundry usability from object bounds.
findings.nextAcceptance: Sample actual washer/dryer door swings with basket, housekeeping cabinet, and a standing operator; add garment hang lengths and an arm/reach envelope under the drying rack.

findings.area: 客厅可移动电视停位与后墙低柜
findings.status: the fixed storage is removed from the effective V9 model; current motion sweep therefore has no such obstacle

selectedAccessFaces.mobileTVScreen: -z when parked at rotation 180; stand extends behind the screen toward +z

calculatedConflict.effectiveV9Status: home-design.ts filters living-rear-storage out before motion-model construction, so the base-model overlap is avoided by sacrificing this low cabinet

findings.noChangeBasis: The V9 overlay explicitly removes the low cabinet for mobile-TV movement and records it in storage.removedForMobility. This is a deliberate storage tradeoff; do not report the earlier base-model overlap as a current effective-model collision.
findings.nextAcceptance: Confirm the effective scene contains no remnant of the removed cabinet or its collisionParts and that both screen/PS5 travelling states pass visible-mesh sweep. Review whether the lost 1.6 x 0.35 x 0.8 m storage remains acceptable.

findings.area: 厨房、主卧工作区、客房与阳台上柜
findings.status: access faces are room-facing; frequency and reach need final user validation

selectedAccessFaces.kitchenRuns: +z for rotation 180 runs; +x for rotation 90 sink run
selectedAccessFaces.masterPegboard: -z, removable hooks for headphones/cables/stationery; fixing substrate and loaded projection unverified

findings.nominalStandingPosition: In front of each unit's transformed local -z face; exact x/z are derived from each stored unit center/rotation in storage-design.ts.
findings.calculatedConflict: Cabinet tops range up to y=2.60 m (kitchen and several wall units); kitchen base cabinets begin at y=1.60 m, master-work upper storage at y=1.65 m, and V9 bar storage at y=1.52 m. The master pegboard occupies x=8.1–10.3, z=4.19–4.29, y=0.97–1.53 behind the inline desk. It is assigned for small accessories, but reachable hook spacing, wall fixing, and loaded projection are not calculated. Top-lift doors on the separate upper unit reduce outward swing but do not prove overhead reach or loaded-item safety.
findings.noChangeBasis: The final V9 overlay replaces the entry display shelf and loose hooks with a front-facing pegboard at x=7.3,z=8.29,y=1.24 (0.82 x 0.64 m). The main bedroom adds a 2.2 x 0.56 m pegboard at x=9.2,z=4.24,y=0.97 behind the inline desk; this supports small-item storage without a corner return. High wardrobe/fridge/entry/housekeeping storage remains seasonal.
findings.nextAcceptance: Check daily-item retrieval with the actual user's reach envelope and verify pegboard fixing substrate/load, removable-hook clearances, door operation, and monitor/desk interaction. Separate everyday light items from heavy/seasonal stock; record shelf heights and recoverability without relying on toe-standing unless explicitly accepted.

overallStatus.P0: No new whole-room access P0 confirmed in this read-only pass.
P1: Kitchen sink and cooktop nominal two-person stance circles overlap by the current model calculation.
The conservative 0.45 m-radius master-wardrobe stance circle is 0.14 m wider than the narrowest bed-side gap; ordinary standing usability is not inferred from this check.
P2: Kitchen appliance doors and users are not jointly sampled.
The mobile-TV sweep avoids the base-model rear-storage collision because V9 removes that 1.6 x 0.35 x 0.8 m cabinet; this is a model tradeoff pending storage confirmation.
Reach, door-open, and overhead handling checks remain incomplete for upper cabinets.
The laundry basket is stored inside the housekeeping cabinet; basket retrieval, door opening, and transport to the dining-table folding surface have not been jointly verified.
Balcony washer/dryer operation, cabinet opening, basket retrieval, and use of the dining table as a folding surface need a joint sequence check.
overallStatus.claimBoundary: This is a source-backed access audit, not construction, ergonomic certification, measured survey, or physical-use acceptance.
